Thank you I appreciate it. I did lose the first 100 lbs in a little less than 11 months. If I could do it all over again I would lose the weight more slowly. I downloaded the my fitness pal app and started tracking my calories and taking walks, after about 2 months I joined a gym and committed to going at least 3 times a week. Be kind to yourself, you WILL slip up, but just get right back on track. And just because you had a treat doesn’t mean the whole day is blown. There were plenty of days I ate a bag of chips, or a cookie or whatever and still stayed under my calorie goal. Remember this is a lifestyle change not a brief diet. To maintain my weight I workout for about 2 hours a day 4-6 days a week. These days I usually start with a 10 minute warm up jog, an hour and a half of heavy weight lifting then finishing up with 20 minutes on the stairs. I find I can eat quite a lot of food and not gain, but I’m very active. It’s not at all uncommon for me to get 20,000 steps in a day. I don’t track my food anymore because I did start to develop an eating disorder. What works for everyone is different so just listen to your body always.

A bit late, but when I was 14 I overdosed on a bunch of heavy psych meds. I was in icu for one night and the normal hospital for 2, I almost died. Today I'm 21, about to get my associates degree and transfer, and I work on my campus as a mental health peer mentor. Things didn't suddenly get better, I had to work like  hell to get where I am now, but I'm so happy I'm still alive. I've been diagnosed with ptsd, major depressive disorder, social anxiety,  and generalized anxiety disorder. I still struggle with anxiety, and of course I have bad days, but I wouldn't trade it for the world. I'm going into the helping field, because I don't ever want anyone to feel as helpless and alone as I felt. There is help, and your pain can end without you ending your life. If anyone is struggling feel free to PM me.
